title: 2018 AMC 10B Problem 2
statement: Sam drove \(96\) miles in \(90\) minutes. His average speed during the first \(30\) minutes was \(60\) mph (miles per hour), and his average speed during the second \(30\) minutes was \(65\) mph. What was his average speed, in mph, during the last \(30\) minutes?

solutions.text: Each leg is half an hour. In the first, Sam drove \(60 \cdot \tfrac12 = 30\) miles; in the second, \(65 \cdot \tfrac12 = 32.5\) miles. That’s \(62.5\) miles so far. That leaves \(96 - 62.5 = 33.5\) miles for the last half hour, which is a speed of \(\frac{33.5}{\tfrac12} = 67\) mph. Therefore, the answer is D.
hints: Distance = rate \(\times\) time, and each \(30\)-minute leg is half an hour
Subtract the distance covered in the first hour from \(96\) to get the last leg’s distance
